pr.title: Remove Rvalue::Len again.
pr.description:
Now that we have `RawPtrKind::FakeForPtrMetadata`, we can reimplement `Rvalue::Len` using `PtrMetadata(&raw const (fake) place)`.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR is a MIR-representation refactor: it removes `Rvalue::Len` and re-expresses length reads as `UnOp::PtrMetadata` on a fake raw pointer. The only historical wrong/incomplete behavior identified by the frozen analysis is that the new `PtrMetadata` form is not folded by GVN/DataflowConstProp (e.g. an array-to-slice unsizing cast's metadata remains opaque instead of becoming `const N`). That is explicitly a missed optimization, not a semantic change: the runtime value of `PtrMetadata` of the unsized pointer is still the array length, and the generated bounds checks still compare the same values. Thus there is no source-grounded pair of functions whose defined executions produce different original/transformed results. Producing different values would require the unrelated, over-broad rewrite that folds metadata of arbitrary slice pointers to an array length; that hypothetical unsound transformation is not what this PR historically did, and the instructions forbid manufacturing it just to obtain a difference.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, MIR represented a length read as `Rvalue::Len(place)`. GVN had a dedicated `Value::Len(VnIndex)` and `simplify_len`: it immediately folded an array place using its type length (`// Trivial case: we are fetching a statically known length.`), otherwise walked deref-only reborrows and an unsizing cast from `[T; N]` to `[T]`, and used `// Fallback: a symbolic `Len`.` DataflowConstProp handled `Rvalue::Len(place)` directly: for `ty::Array(_, len)` it evaluated the type-level length, for a deref-only place it used `state.get_len(place.local.into(), &self.map)`, and otherwise produced `FlatSet::Top`. After this PR, `Rvalue::Len` no longer exists; the same information is obtained from `UnOp::PtrMetadata` on a fake raw pointer, so passes that folded `Len` must fold the corresponding `PtrMetadata` instead.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong/incomplete behavior for the new representation is to retain only the old `Rvalue::Len` folding logic: `PtrMetadata` of a wide pointer produced by an array-to-slice unsizing cast then remains opaque instead of being replaced by the array length. In GVN that means `_0 = PtrMetadata(move _4)` is not rewritten to `_0 = const 42_usize`; in DataflowConstProp the metadata read is not propagated, so a subsequent bounds check is not changed to a constant comparison. This is a missed optimization, not a demonstrated miscompile. Equally, an over-broad rewrite that folds metadata of any slice pointer to an array length would be unsound; folding is valid only when the pointer's metadata demonstrably comes from an `[T; N]`-to-`[T]` unsizing cast (possibly through metadata-preserving pointer casts and reborrows).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR length/metadata reads: `Rvalue::Len(place)` in the old representation, or `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::PtrMetadata, operand)` in the new representation. Relevant sources are arrays `[T; N]` with type-level length N, wide pointers/slices whose metadata is known from an unsizing cast `&[T; N]`/`*const [T; N]` to `&[T]`/`*const [T]`, and chains of deref-only reborrows or `PtrToPtr` casts that preserve pointer metadata. Inputs whose slice length comes from a function argument or an opaque pointer are in the domain but must not be folded to a constant.
analysis.summary: Removing `Rvalue::Len` and re-expressing length reads as `PtrMetadata(&raw const (fake) place)` requires GVN and DataflowConstProp to move their old `Len` folding over to `PtrMetadata`. GVN must peel metadata-preserving PtrToPtr casts and deref-only reborrows, and recognize an array-to-slice unsizing cast as a constant length; DataflowConstProp must use `map.find_len` when the `PtrMetadata` operand is a place, otherwise fall back to ordinary operand evaluation. The added MIR tests assert that array lengths become constants while genuine runtime slice lengths remain `PtrMetadata`.
analysis.trigger: A program indexes or takes the length of an array or a slice whose wide-pointer metadata originated from an array unsizing cast, for example `(&[1u32, 2, 3] as &[u32])[1]`, `const SLICE: &[u32] = &[1, 2, 3]`, or a promoted array reference passed through `PtrMetadata`. The same transformations must not fire when the slice length is only known at runtime.
preconditions: The `PtrMetadata` operand must be traceable to a place or pointer value whose length is known.

For GVN's unsize rule, the cast must be `CastKind::PointerCoercion(ty::adjustment::PointerCoercion::Unsize, _)`, the source pointee must be `ty::Array(_, len)`, and the destination pointee must be `ty::Slice(..)`.
Pointer casts may be peeled only when they preserve metadata, and reborrow peeling is limited to deref-only projections.
For DataflowConstProp, length lookup via `find_len` requires an actual place operand; otherwise the normal operand/unary-op evaluation path must still run.
pitfalls: Do not treat `PtrMetadata` as a place-only rvalue in DataflowConstProp: `operand.place()` may be absent, so the old unary-op evaluation must remain as a fallback.
Do not fold every `PtrMetadata`; the array-to-slice unsize rule must check both the source array and destination slice.
Do not peel arbitrary casts while walking metadata; only metadata-preserving PtrToPtr casts and deref-only reborrows are valid.
In the GVN loop, each match must update `arg_index` and continue from the updated index, with `was_updated` set after the match, rather than breaking after the first rewrite.

Do not assume `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` of a local can remain nop'ed merely because the length became constant; the new raw-pointer/PtrMetadata chain can keep locals referenced, as reflected in the GVN test diff changes from `+ nop;` back to retained storage statements.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR-opt regression tests for both representations' replacement behavior. Use `//@ test-mir-pass: DataflowConstProp`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_BIT_WIDTH`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, and emit per-pass diffs. Cover an array pattern `[a, b, rest @ .., e]` with CHECK-NOT for both `Len` and `PtrMetadata` and CHECK for `= const 5_usize`, and a slice pattern with `// CHECK: = PtrMetadata(copy _1);`. For DataflowConstProp, use a promoted array unsized to a slice and a named const slice; assert CHECK-NOT for `Len`/`Lt`/`assert(move _`, CHECK `const 3_usize` and `const true`, and CHECK indexing becomes `[1 of 2]`. Keep a runtime slice-parameter case to ensure runtime metadata is not replaced by a constant. Add execution-level assertions such as `assert_eq!(norm2([3.0, 4.0]), 5.0 * 5.0);` and the `normN` equivalent, while relying on MIR checks for the optimization itself. Include both panic-abort and panic-unwind and both 32-bit and 64-bit expectations where the test harness supports them.
evidence: Now that we have `RawPtrKind::FakeForPtrMetadata`, we can reimplement `Rvalue::Len` using `PtrMetadata(&raw const (fake) place)`.
